claims.content: Customer successfully places a bid on an auction item using an available bidding mechanism (e.g., SmartBid, Single Bid, or QuickBid Now/standard bidding).

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer places a bid on an auction item through one of the available bidding options.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: A customer selects an auction item, chooses one bidding mechanism (such as SmartBid, Single Bid, or QuickBid Now/standard bidding), and successfully submits a bid for that item.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The customer initiates the bid-placing action on an auction item.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The bid has been placed on the auction item through the selected bidding mechanism.
in_scope_actions: Selecting a bidding option (SmartBid, Single Bid, or QuickBid Now/standard bidding)
Submitting/placing the bid on the auction item
excluded_adjacent_actions: Auction item administration or listing maintenance
variant_dimensions: Bid option type: SmartBid, Single Bid, or QuickBid Now/standard bidding

claims.content: Customer
The auction item is active/open for bidding: the system has been configured to accept bids on it, it is past the Preview Period, is not closed, and is displaying remaining bidding time.
The auction item is listed/visible in the system with its bidding configuration defined (cost tier, opening bid/reserve amount, and bid increments).

The use case is triggered when the customer clicks a bid control for an auction item: the 'QuickBid'/'QuickBid Now' button to place an immediate single incremental bid, or the SmartBid/Single Bid option followed by the corresponding 'Place SmartBid'/'Place Single Bid' button, from either the list view or the Product Details page.

The customer selects a bidding mechanism by entering a bid amount into the SmartBid or Single Bid input field and clicking the 'Place SmartBid' or 'Place Single Bid' button, or by clicking the 'QuickBid Now'/'QuickBid' button to initiate the bid.
The system verifies that the bidder is signed in and has the required minimum information before allowing the bid to be placed.
The system displays a bid confirmation popup showing the bid amount, bid type, and payment instrument (e.g., card ending digits); the rest of the page is grayed out and unclickable.
Customer confirms the bid by clicking the confirmation button (e.g., 'Yes, Place SmartBid').

After the bid is placed, the customer remains on the Product Details page for the standard signed-in SmartBid/Single Bid flow and for a signed-in QuickBid; however, if the bid was placed via QuickBid while the user was not signed in, the system redirects the customer to the catalog page.

Diverges from Step 2: If the bidder is not signed in but already has the required minimum information to bid, the system takes the bidder directly to the sign-in page before allowing the bid to be placed; after signing in, the system returns the bidder to the Product Details page of the item they initially tried to bid on, and the bid placement proceeds.

Diverges from Step 2: If the user is not signed in when clicking the QuickBid button, the system prompts them to sign in and, after successful authentication, returns them to the catalog page, completing the QuickBid placement.
Diverges from main flow Step 2: If the user is not signed in when clicking the QuickBid button, the system prompts them to sign in; exit: after sign-in, the user is redirected to the catalog page.

Diverges from main flow Step 2: If the user is not signed in when clicking anywhere within the product module (except QuickBid), the system presents a sign-in page; exit: after sign-in completion, the user is redirected to the Product Details page.

Diverges from main flow Step 2: If, after the sign-in check, the bidder does not have the required minimum information required to bid, the bid cannot be placed; the system only defines a return to the Product Details page for bidders who do have that information, so the exception exits the use case without placing a bid.
The system updates the Item Bid History for the auction item to record the confirmed bid, including bidder member ID, bid amount, and bid time.

After successful bid placement, the customer is on the Product Details page for non-QuickBid paths: the customer remains there after bid confirmation, and if the non-QuickBid path required sign-in, the system delivers the customer to that page.
After successful bid placement via QuickBid when the user was not signed in, the system redirects the customer to the catalog page.
If the bid triggers overtime bidding, the Product Details page displays the 'OVERTIME BIDDING IS ON!' status message.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Main Flow step 2 requires the system to verify that the bidder is signed in before allowing the bid to be placed. This makes an unsigned QuickBid unable to produce a successful bid, yet Main Flow step 5 and Postcondition 3 define a successful unsigned QuickBid outcome that redirects the customer to the catalog page. That postcondition is therefore not reachable from the preceding main flow guard.

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The Trigger explicitly allows the customer to click the bid control from either the list view or the Product Details page. The final Main Flow step and Postconditions only define after-bid states for PDP-origin flows (remaining on the PDP) and for unsigned QuickBid (redirect to catalog). A signed-in QuickBid initiated from the list view has no defined downstream state, so the vertical flow is incomplete for a trigger variant.

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger fires when the customer clicks the bid control (or clicks Place after selecting SmartBid/Single Bid), but Main Flow step 1 reaches back before the Trigger by having the customer enter a bid amount into the SmartBid/Single Bid input and then click the Place button. The Main Flow should begin after the Trigger click, not restate the pre-trigger entry action.

inconsistency_hints: Main Flow step 5 states unconditionally that after the confirmed bid is placed the customer remains on the Product Details page. This does not reach the postcondition state described for QuickBid when the user was not signed in, where the system redirects the customer to the catalog page; it also ignores the trigger's list-view source and sign-in delivery variants.

Main Flow step 1 duplicates the Trigger: the Trigger already has the customer clicking QuickBid Now or selecting a SmartBid/Single Bid option and clicking the Place button. Step 1 says the customer selects a mechanism and initiates a bid, so it does not pick up after the trigger; it restates it.

The exception flow does not contain any branch for the missing-minimum-bidder-info condition raised by main_flow Step 2. Since the branch is absent, there is no clear exit defined for bidders who lack the required minimum information.

Main Flow step 4 defines post-bid navigation only for SmartBid/Single Bid signed-in flow and for QuickBid when the user was not signed in. The Trigger explicitly includes QuickBid as a mechanism, so a signed-in user can also trigger it; that branch has no defined continuation in the Main Flow, and there is no corresponding postcondition for it.

Main flow is missing the Customer's initiating action: it starts with the system's sign-in/minimum-information check and never shows the Customer selecting a bidding mechanism (SmartBid, Single Bid, or QuickBid) and initiating the bid. This leaves the goal's in-scope action 'Selecting a bidding option' uncovered. The same omission is the underlying cause of the branch-alignment problem: alternative/exception flows refer to 'Step 2' for sign-in-related branches, but in the current main flow that check is Step 1 and Step 2 is the confirmation popup; adding an initiation step and renumbering would make those references consistent.
